subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Opening and Closing Accounts
description: A micro-lesson that makes Opening and Closing Accounts usable.

hook.text: You hold onto a losing stock because selling it closes the mental account at a loss. Keeping it open preserves hope.

buildup.text: Closing a mental account at a loss triggers regret and finality. Keeping it open means the outcome is still 'pending.'

discovery.text: This is why people refuse to sell houses below purchase price, even when holding costs more than the difference.

twist.text: But closing a winning account feels great. This is why people sell winning investments too early: to feel the pleasure.

climax.text: The key insight: the mental account is not the investment. Close accounts based on future prospects, not past results.

punchline.text: Close the account. Keep the lesson.

quiz.question: Why do people avoid selling losing investments?
options: Closing the mental account at a loss triggers regret
Tax laws prevent selling at a loss
